title: Commune of the Zealots
capsule: The Zealots were a popular-revolutionary faction in Thessaloniki who seized power in 1342 amid the broader civil war between John VI Kantakouzenos and the regency for John V Palaiologos. Drawing support from artisans and sailors against the local aristocracy, they established a commune that expelled or killed the city's nobility and governed Thessaloniki independently for nearly a decade, reportedly maintaining contact with the Serbian court and Genoese interests. The commune's power waned after 1349 when John VI Kantakouzenos consolidated control; by 1350 the Zealots had been suppressed and the city reintegrated into the Byzantine state under the Empress Anna of Savoy's party.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Zealot commune controlled the city of Thessaloniki itself, but the spatial extent of their effective authority in the surrounding countryside is poorly documented and likely fluctuated throughout the 1344–1352 window.
